name: Variegated Face Emotion Retrieval
description: Automatic facial emotion recognition, despite deep learning advancements, faces challenges with large manually annotated datasets and demographic imbalance. While visual-language models (VLMs) show promise in aligning visual and textual emotion data, content-based facial emotion retrieval is underexplored, and larger models exhibit demographic sensitivity. This study introduces Facial INtensity of Emotions (FINE), the first large-scale dataset balancing gender, race, and Ekman's six emotions, across four intensity of emotion levels. We propose a retrieval protocol and baseline using fine-tuned contrastive language-image pre-training-based VLMs, demonstrating that fine-tuning on FINE consistently improves accuracy and reduces performance variance across demographics and emotion classes, thereby mitigating representation bias. However, misclassification rates still increase at the highest intensity levels even after fine-tuning, indicating expression magnitude remains an open challenge. This work confirms fine-tuning's value in enhancing generalization and reducing variability in emotion retrieval, establishing FINE as a robust benchmark.
reputation: Very recent (2025) benchmark; currently limited adoption outside the authors' community.
notes: Multimodal retrieval benchmark involving faces and emotion labels — raises privacy and bias concerns. Likely limited scale and early-stage adoption; non-LLM benchmark.
